update() runs synchronously on every window "resize" event (its own listener, not rAF-throttled; slider.js:94). (1) scrollable = scrollWidth - clientWidth > 4 shows or hides both arrows and the dots row (display "" / none). (2) prev.disabled = scrollLeft <= 2 and next.disabled = scrollLeft >= scrollWidth - clientWidth - 2, where disabled = opacity 0 + pointer-events none, faded over .15s. (3) Dots = max(1, ceil((scrollWidth-4)/clientWidth)); when the count changes the row is emptied and rebuilt with new buttons. (4) The active dot = last when at the end, else round(scrollLeft/clientWidth). MEASURED, both tracks, resizing a live page 1440 -> 744 -> 390 -> 1440: columns 300 -> 258 -> 258 -> 300px; scrollWidth/clientWidth 2540/1360 -> 2204/685 -> 2204/358 -> 2540/1360; dots 2 -> 4 -> 7 -> 2; arrows stay shown, prev disabled at scrollLeft 0, next enabled.

behaviour.action: window resize wider than the content
behaviour.expected: MEASURED at 2800px: the track stays 1360px wide (section max-width) and 2540px of content, so it is still scrollable with 2 dots. On home the "hide arrows and dots" branch is never reached by resizing (8 cards always overflow).

MEASURED: #recTrack at its end at 1440 (scrollLeft 1180, next disabled, dot 2/2 active), then resized to 744: scrollLeft stays 1180 (max is now 1519), so next is re-enabled (opacity 1), prev stays enabled, the row rebuilds to 4 dots and dot 3 (index round(1180/685)=2) is active. If a resize lowers the max scroll, the clamp also fires a scroll event, so the rAF update runs as well.

each enhance() adds a window resize listener that is never removed. The engine re-render replaced the first track, so its old arrow pair and dots row stay in the host. Their update() runs against the detached track (scrollWidth = clientWidth = 0) and keeps them display:none with 1 dot. MEASURED: 4 arrow buttons per host (2 hidden) and 1 hidden 1-dot row.
